description: DECISIONS.md 2026-11-06): the electric module's tray and duct box with nothing in it. Part of every build; the first stage of every commissioning. The lines below point at bom/heat-electric-240.csv so the two cannot drift apart. Nothing electrical.

generic_spec: Exactly HE-TRAY in heat-electric-240.csv: the laser-cut 340 x 280 x 1.5 tray (mechanical/drawings/heat-module-tray.dxf), on the 2020 tray rails from Y 420 to 700 with four M4 T-nuts, with its M6 bonding stud (the box is bonded even with nothing electrical in it, so an element added later needs no new stud)
notes: cut once; an electric build reuses this tray

description: Element box plates without the terminal plate
generic_spec: HE-BOX less the terminal plate: the four walls and the lid (mechanical/drawings/heat-module-wall-left.dxf, -right, -front, -rear, heat-module-top.dxf), joined with the twelve CH-ANGLE-20 pieces and M4 button heads as in heat-electric-240.csv; the element rails, the terminal plate and its foot angle are left out; the 40 x 25 terminal opening in the right wall and the two thermostat bracket hole pairs in the lid stay open (they are inside the louvered bay and draw only room air)
notes: an electric build adds the element rails, the element, the thermostats and the terminal plate to this same box; nothing is recut

generic_spec: Exactly HE-COLLAR: the 125 flanged starting collar cut to stand 55.5 above the lid, 3 under the riser's hood
The box's 64 M4 x 8 button heads and 60 nuts and the collar's 4 M4 from CH-BOLT-M4; the four M4 T-nuts from CH-TNUT-M4; the M6 bonding stud, two nuts and star washers
notes: no element, no thermostats, no DIN rail, no devices, no wire

vendor_2_part_number: HE-WIRE and the element rails. The common power module's heat-enable chain stays fitted (design-rules section 4) so a heat module can be slid in later.
